"Let me tell you why we should settle only for legalization, and not decriminalization."
A Reader In New York Makes A Valuable Point, Learned The Hard Way.

(Marijuananews note: I very strongly believe that just "decriminalizing"possession is completely inadequate. We need full legalization of cultivation, sale and possession.)

Why Cultivation And Sale of Marijuana Must Be Legalized;
But That Definitely Was Not The Intended Message!

May 10, 1999

Dear Mr. Cowan:

Let me tell you why we should settle only for legalization, and not decriminalization.

I am a resident of New York City, where marijuana was supposed to have been basically decriminalized in the early 1970s. But just because that is what they say, does not mean it is true.

I am a senior in college, majoring in Finance and Economics, and am basically a law abiding citizen (if you don’t include my marijuana smoking). Last November, I was picked up by the NYPD for possession of a small bag of marijuana (about 1.5 grams), handcuffed, put in a van, and drove around for about six hours while these officers were looking for other marijuana users.
(Marijuananews note: What a total waste of police resources!)
We were taken to central booking, and needless to say, I spend close to 24 hours in police custody. I was charged with a Class E Felony (this in a state that is supposed to have a form of decriminalization).
See

Are people really being arrested for marijuana possession? What happens when someone is arrested?

Why Cultivation And Sale of Marijuana Must Be Legalized;
But That Definitely Was Not The Intended Message!

May 10, 1999

Dear Mr. Cowan:

Let me tell you why we should settle only for legalization, and not decriminalization.

I am a resident of New York City, where marijuana was supposed to have been basically decriminalized in the early 1970s. But just because that is what they say, does not mean it is true.

I am a senior in college, majoring in Finance and Economics, and am basically a law abiding citizen (if you don’t include my marijuana smoking). Last November, I was picked up by the NYPD for possession of a small bag of marijuana (about 1.5 grams), handcuffed, put in a van, and drove around for about six hours while these officers were looking for other marijuana users.
(Marijuananews note: What a total waste of police resources!)
We were taken to central booking, and needless to say, I spend close to 24 hours in police custody. I was charged with a Class E Felony (this in a state that is supposed to have a form of decriminalization).
See

Lucky for me, this was the only time I have ever been arrested in my life. I was given an Adjournment in Contemplation of Dismissal (ACD), which is basically a form of probation that stipulates that as long as I remain crime free (I was told that traffic tickets count as well), I will have the case dropped. But get into trouble, and I will be a convicted felon. And had I had any other trouble with law enforcement before, even an other misdemeanor, I would now be a convicted felon, and kiss any future career in finance goodbye.

This is why I think people should never settle for decriminalization, and should instead aim for full legalization.

You can use this letter in your web site if you wish, but please do not use my name at the present time for obvious reasons.

Sincerely,

Rudolf Giuliani, Jr.
(Marijuananews note: Only kidding!

When requested, or even when it just seems appropriate, I always protect the confidentiality of correspondents.

It is obvious from this well-written letter that society would be much the poorer if the author had been kept from reaching his full potential. The damage done to people who have arrest records is another of the hidden costs of marijuana prohibition.)
